N006 applies on [a,t], length at most tau<=1, with slot i=3: constant f has X norm ||f||_2<=M0+1 and Y has X norm O(q) and negative norm O(tau*q). In S003 symmetry places Y' in the asymmetric J estimate, requiring only Dinv Y', not an unavailable L2 bound on Y'. In S004 each w=v(t_n), f=v^n satisfies F003 at the intersected step start. Differentiating D022 gives Vst'=(1/2)B(z,z)-W/tau; expansion of Vst=z+Y yields the displayed residual derivative. N005 bounds it in H^(-pstar) by O(q+q^2)=O(q). For integral B(Y,z), normal-form boundary and Y' terms are O(tau*q), and N006 bounds the remaining cubic term by O(tau*q). The analogous Y,Y terms are O(tau*q^2), reduced using q<=2; W has size O(tau*q). Summing at most h/tau+1 step increments proves the residual estimate, including a partial last step. Finally e'=B(e,v-e/2)-Rres', ||e||_2<=E_I and bounded ||v-e/2||_2 give ||e'||_(H^(-pstar))=O(tau^gamma+E_I). D017 then gives the asserted X bounds, including those for v and V. Only smooth differentiation, norm integration and finite concatenation occur; no unsupported limiting exchange is needed.
